mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% over the prior quarter reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by at least 0.25% in a consecutive monthly pattern for 3 months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during the 30-day pre-trend window (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate falls below 5% for the first time in a 6-month window, wage growth expectations for the coming quarter increase, boosting S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses below 5% in a single month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns under this regime are not statistically higher than during the prior 20-day period with UNRATE > 5% (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the HOUST index of home sales exceeding 3% for two consecutive months indicates accelerating household demand, which elevates equity valuations and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by more than 3% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not positive when the trigger is met (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in the INDPRO index (manufacturing production) of more than 2% in a single month coincides with a 10-day window of declining S&P 500 forward returns as investor confidence weakens.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by more than 2% in a single month
failure_condition: 10-day forward returns remain consistently positive despite the production drop (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive monthly declines in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL by at least 0.2% each create a dual signal of tightening and higher inflation expectations, which together produce negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS decreases while CPIAUCSL decreases in the same month for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during the prior 20-day window with no such dual decline (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When monthly PAYEMS exceeds 160,000 by 10% year-over-year, it signals strong labor market momentum that supports equity risk appetite and drives positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns under this trigger are not significantly higher than the prior 60-day average (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 4-week moving average of GDPC1 (real private consumption) growing at a rate exceeding 3% monthly predicts strong demand momentum that will produce positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive when the 4-week MA crosses the threshold (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a regime where FEDFUNDS remains above 5% for 3 consecutive months and UNRATE stays below 5%, S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days are typically negative due to persistent risk aversion.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not consistently negative across 10 such regimes (p > 0.05).
